text: Dimensions of universal gravitational constant ($G$) in terms of Planck's constant ($h$), distance ($L$), mass ($M$) and time ($T$) are $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the dimensions of the universal gravitational constant G in terms of Planck's constant h , length L , mass M , and time T , we must first determine the base dimensions of both G and h in the standard MLT system.

According to Newton's law of universal gravitation, the force F between two masses $\mathrm{m}_{1}$ and $\mathrm{m}_{2}$ separated by a distance $r$ is given by:

$\mathrm{F}=\frac{\mathrm{Gm}_{1}\mathrm{m}_{2}}{\mathrm{r}^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \mathrm{G}=\frac{\mathrm{Fr}^{2}}{\mathrm{m}_{1}\mathrm{m}_{2}}$

Substituting the dimensions $\left [MLT^{-2}\right ]$ for force, $[L]$ for distance $(r)$, and mass( $m$ ) as $[M]$ :

$[\mathrm{G}]=\frac{\left [\mathrm{MLT}^{-2}\right ]\left [\mathrm{L}^{2}\right ]}{[\mathrm{M}][\mathrm{M}]}=\left [\mathrm{M}^{-1}\mathrm{L}^{3}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ]$

Planck's constant relates the energy $E$ of a photon to its frequency $v$ via the equation:

$\mathrm{E}=\mathrm{h}ν$

Since frequency $v$ has dimensions of inverse time [ $\mathrm{T}^{-1}$ ], and energy E (work done) has dimensions $\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ]$, we have:

$[\mathrm{h}]=\frac{[\mathrm{E}]}{[\mathrm{v}]}=\frac{\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ]}{[\mathrm{T}^{-1}]}=\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-1}\right ]$

Let assume the relationship is of the form $\mathrm{G}=\mathrm{h}^{\mathrm{a}}\mathrm{L}^{\mathrm{b}}\mathrm{M}^{\mathrm{c}}\mathrm{T}^{\mathrm{d}}$. Comparing the dimensions:

$\left [\mathrm{M}^{-1}\mathrm{L}^{3}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ]=\left [\mathrm{ML}^{2}\mathrm{T}^{-1}\right ]^{\mathrm{a}}[\mathrm{L}]^{\mathrm{b}}[\mathrm{M}]^{\mathrm{c}}[\mathrm{T}]^{\mathrm{d}}$

$\left [\mathrm{M}^{-1}\mathrm{L}^{3}\mathrm{T}^{-2}\right ]=\left [\mathrm{M}^{\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{c}}\mathrm{L}^{2\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}}\mathrm{T}^{-\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{d}}\right ]$

By equating the exponents of $\mathrm{M},\mathrm{L}$, and T from both sides, we get a system of equations:

For $\mathrm{M}:\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{c}=-1\ldots$ (i)

For $\mathrm{L}:2\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}=3\ldots$ (ii)

For $\mathrm{T}:-\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{d}=-2\ldots$ (iii)

Looking at the provided options, we see that h is with a power of $1,\mathrm{a}=1$

Let's $\mathrm{a}=1$ :

From eq (i): $1+\mathrm{c}=-1\Rightarrow \mathrm{c}=-2$

From eq (ii): $2(1)+b=3\Rightarrow b=1$

From eq (iii): $-1+\mathrm{d}=-2\Rightarrow \mathrm{d}=-1$

Substituting these values, we get $G\propto h^{1}L^{1}M^{-2}T^{-1}$. This corresponds to the dimensional formula $\left [\mathrm{hT}^{-1}\mathrm{LM}^{-2}\right ]$. 

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: A 0.5 kg mass is in contact against the inner wall of a cylindrical drum of radius 4 m rotating about its vertical axis. The minimum rotational speed of the drum to enable the mass to remain stuck to the wall (without falling) is 5 rad/s. The coefficient of friction between the drum’s inner wall surface and mass is $_________. ($Take $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the frame of the drum the mass is at rest under four forces: the normal force $N$ from the wall towards the axis, the centrifugal force $mω^{2}r$ away from the axis, the weight $mg$ downwards and static friction $f_{s}$ upwards.


[IMG]

Radial balance gives $N=mω^{2}r$; vertical balance gives $f_{s}=mg$, with $f_{s}\leq μN$.

At the minimum angular speed, friction is limiting:

$μmω^{2}r=mg\Rightarrow μ=\dfrac{g}{ω^{2}r}=\dfrac{10}{5^{2}\times 4}=0.1$

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
Two blocks of masses 2 kg and 1 kg respectively, are tied to the ends of a string which passes over a light frictionless pulley as shown in the figure below. The masses are held at rest at the same horizontal level and then released. The distance traversed by the centre of mass in 2 s is $_______ m. ($Take $g=10m/s^{2}$)

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $\mathrm{m}_{1}=2\mathrm{kg}$ and $\mathrm{m}_{2}=1\mathrm{kg}$. When released, the heavier mass moves downward and the lighter mass moves upward with the same magnitude of acceleration a.

As the string connecting two blocks is massless, so tension throughout will be same, T .


[IMG]


For block $\mathrm{m}_{1}$, using Newton's $2^{\text{nd}}$ law of motion;

$\mathrm{m}_{1}\mathrm{g}-\mathrm{T}=\mathrm{m}_{1}\mathrm{a}\ldots (\mathrm{i})$

For block $\mathrm{m}_{2}$, using Newton's $2^{\text{nd}}$ law of motion;

$\mathrm{T}-\mathrm{m}_{2}\mathrm{g}=\mathrm{m}_{2}\mathrm{a}...(ii)$

Adding both the equations,

$(m_{1}-m_{2})g=(m_{1}+m_{2})a$

$a=\left (\frac{m_{1}-m_{2}}{m_{1}+m_{2}}\right )g$

Substituting the given values $\left (\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}\right )$ :

$\mathrm{a}=\left (\frac{2-1}{2+1}\right )\times 10=\frac{1}{3}\times 10=\frac{10}{3}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$

The acceleration of the centre of mass for a two-body system is defined as :

$\vec{\mathrm{a}}_{\mathrm{cm}}=\frac{\mathrm{m}_{1}\vec{\mathrm{a}}_{1}+\mathrm{m}_{2}\vec{\mathrm{a}}_{2}}{\mathrm{m}_{1}+\mathrm{m}_{2}}$

Taking the downward direction as positive :

$\vec{\mathrm{a}}_{1}=\mathrm{a}$ (downward)

$\vec{\mathrm{a}}_{2}=-\mathrm{a}$ (upward)

$\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{cm}}=\frac{\mathrm{m}_{1}(\mathrm{a})+\mathrm{m}_{2}(-\mathrm{a})}{\mathrm{m}_{1}+\mathrm{m}_{2}}=\left (\frac{\mathrm{m}_{1}-\mathrm{m}_{2}}{\mathrm{m}_{1}+\mathrm{m}_{2}}\right )\mathrm{a}$

Substituting the value of a :

$\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{cm}}=\left (\frac{2-1}{2+1}\right )\times \frac{10}{3}=\frac{1}{3}\times \frac{10}{3}=\frac{10}{9}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$

The system starts from rest ( $\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{cm}}=0$ ). The distance traversed in time $\mathrm{t}=2\mathrm{s}$ is given by the kinematic equation :

$\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cm}}=\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{cm}}\mathrm{t}+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{cm}}\mathrm{t}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cm}}=0+\frac{1}{2}\left (\frac{10}{9}\right )(2)^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{cm}}=\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{10}{9}\times 4=\frac{20}{9}\approx 2.22\mathrm{m}$

Therefore, the correct option is (C).

text: A particle having charge $10^{-9}$ C moving in $x$-$y$ plane in fields of $0.4\hat{j}$ N/C and $4\times 10^{-3}\hat{k}$ T experiences a force of $(4\hat{i}+2\hat{j})\times 10^{-10}$ N. The velocity of the particle at that instant is $_________ m/s$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The force on the charge is $⃗{F}=q\left (⃗{E}+⃗{v}\times ⃗{B}\right )$ with $q=10^{-9}\text{C}$, $⃗{E}=0.4\hat{j}\text{N C}^{-1}$, $⃗{B}=4\times 10^{-3}\hat{k}\text{T}$ and, for motion in the $x$-$y$ plane, $⃗{v}=v_{x}\hat{i}+v_{y}\hat{j}$.

Using $\hat{i}\times \hat{k}=-\hat{j}$ and $\hat{j}\times \hat{k}=\hat{i}$:

$⃗{v}\times ⃗{B}=4\times 10^{-3}v_{y}\hat{i}-4\times 10^{-3}v_{x}\hat{j}$

Dividing the force by $q$:

$\dfrac{⃗{F}}{q}=\dfrac{(4\hat{i}+2\hat{j})\times 10^{-10}}{10^{-9}}=0.4\hat{i}+0.2\hat{j}$

Equating with $⃗{E}+⃗{v}\times ⃗{B}$:

$0.4\hat{i}+0.2\hat{j}=4\times 10^{-3}v_{y}\hat{i}+\left (0.4-4\times 10^{-3}v_{x}\right )\hat{j}$

Along $\hat{i}$: $4\times 10^{-3}v_{y}=0.4\Rightarrow v_{y}=100\text{m s}^{-1}$.

Along $\hat{j}$: $0.4-4\times 10^{-3}v_{x}=0.2\Rightarrow v_{x}=50\text{m s}^{-1}$.

So $⃗{v}=\left (50\hat{i}+100\hat{j}\right )\text{m s}^{-1}$.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text:
If a body of mass 1 kg falls on the earth from infinity, it attains velocity (v) and kinetic energy (k) on reaching the surface of earth. The values of v and k respectively are $__________$.

(Take radius of earth to be 6400 km and $g = 9.8 m/s^{2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let M be the mass of the Earth, R be its radius, and m be the mass of the body ( 1 kg ).

At infinity ( $\mathrm{r}=\infty$ ) the potential energy ( $\mathrm{U}_{\infty }$ ) is 0 , and since it falls (starts from rest), the kinetic energy ( $\mathrm{K}_{\infty }$ ) is 0 .

Hence, total energy at infinity (initial) is $\mathrm{E}_{1}=\mathrm{K}_{1}+\mathrm{U}_{1}=0$.

At Earth's surface $(\mathrm{r}=\mathrm{R})$ the potential energy is $\mathrm{U}=-\frac{\mathrm{GMm}}{\mathrm{R}}$ and the kinetic energy is $\mathrm{K}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{mv}^{2}$.

Hence, total energy at Earth surface (final) is $\mathrm{E}_{2}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{mv}^{2}-\frac{\mathrm{GMm}}{\mathrm{R}}$.

By conservation of energy ( $\mathrm{E}_{1}=\mathrm{E}_{2}$ ) :

$0=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{mv}^{2}-\frac{\mathrm{GMm}}{\mathrm{R}}\Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{mv}^{2}=\frac{\mathrm{GMm}}{\mathrm{R}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $v=\sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}}$

We know that acceleration due to gravity is $\mathrm{g}=\frac{\mathrm{GM}}{\mathrm{R}^{2}}$, so $\mathrm{GM}=\mathrm{gR}^{2}$.

Substituting into the expression for speed,

$v=\sqrt{\frac{2(gR^{2})}{R}}=\sqrt{2gR}$

The acceleration due to gravity at Earth's surface is $\mathrm{g}=9.8\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$ and the radius of Earth is $\mathrm{R}=6400\mathrm{km}=6.4\times 10^{6}\mathrm{m}$.

Putting the values,

$v=\sqrt{2\times 9.8\times 6.4\times 10^{6}}=\sqrt{125.44\times 10^{6}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{v}=11.2\times 10^{3}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}=11.2\mathrm{km}/\mathrm{s}$

The kinetic energy k at the surface is given by :

$\mathrm{k}=\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{mv}^{2}$

Substituting $\mathrm{m}=1\mathrm{kg}$ and $\mathrm{v}=11.2\times 10^{3}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ :

$\mathrm{k}=\frac{1}{2}\times 1\times \left (11.2\times 10^{3}\right )^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{k}=0.5\times 125.44\times 10^{6}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{k}=62.72\times 10^{6}\mathrm{J}=6.27\times 10^{7}\mathrm{J}$

Hence, at the surface of Earth, the values of v and k respectively are $11.2\mathrm{km}/\mathrm{s},6.27\times 10^{7}\mathrm{J}$. 

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: In a screw gauge the zero of main scale reference line coincides with the fifth division of the circular scale when two studs are in contact. There are 100 divisions in circular scale and pitch of screw gauge is 0.1 mm. When diameter of a sphere is measured, the reading of main scale is 5 mm and $50^{th}$ division of circular scale coincides with the reference line of main scale. The diameter of sphere is $______ mm$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The least count is the smallest distance the screw moves when the circular scale is rotated by one division. It is defined as:

$\text{Least Count}=\frac{\text{Pitch}}{\text{Number of divisions on circular scale}}$

The pitch is linear distance moved in one complete rotation. The pitch of screw gauge is given as 0.1 mm and there are 100 divisions:

So, the least count is $\mathrm{LC}=\frac{0.1\mathrm{mm}}{100}=0.001\mathrm{mm}$

When the studs are in contact, the 5th division of the circular scale coincides with the reference line. Since the zero of the circular scale has passed the reference line, the error is positive.

Zero Error $=+($ Coinciding division $\times$ LC $)$

$\Rightarrow$ Zero Error $=+(5\times 0.001\mathrm{mm})=+0.005\mathrm{mm}$

The total observed reading is the sum of the Main Scale Reading (MSR) and the Circular Scale Reading (CSR).

$\mathrm{MSR}=5\mathrm{mm}$

CSR $=$ Coinciding circular division × LC $=50\times 0.001\mathrm{mm}=0.05\mathrm{mm}$

So, observed reading $=5\mathrm{mm}+0.05\mathrm{mm}=5.05\mathrm{mm}$

The true diameter is obtained by subtracting the zero error from the observed reading:

So, the true diameter $=$ Observed Reading - Zero Error

True Diameter $=5.05\mathrm{mm}-0.005\mathrm{mm}=5.045\mathrm{mm}$

Therefore, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift

text: The surface tension of a soap bubble is 0.03 N/m. The work done in increasing the diameter of bubble from 2 cm to 6 cm is $απ\times 10^{-4}$ J. The value of $α$ is $_________. ($Take $π=3.14$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Work done in increasing the size of a soap bubble is stored as surface energy.

A soap bubble has two free surfaces (the inner and the outer air-liquid interfaces). The work done W is given by :

$\mathrm{W}=\mathrm{T}\times (2\times \Delta \mathrm{A})$

Where T is surface tension and $\Delta \mathrm{A}$ is the change in area of one surface

$\Delta A=\left (4πR_{2}^{2}-4πR_{1}^{2}\right )$

Putting the expression in work done,

$\mathrm{W}=2\mathrm{T}\times 4π\left (\mathrm{R}_{2}^{2}-\mathrm{R}_{1}^{2}\right )=8π\mathrm{T}\left (\mathrm{R}_{2}^{2}-\mathrm{R}_{1}^{2}\right )$

The surface tension of soap bubble is $\mathrm{T}=0.03\mathrm{N}/\mathrm{m}$

The initial diameter is $\mathrm{D}_{1}=2\mathrm{cm}\Rightarrow \mathrm{R}_{1}=1\mathrm{cm}=1\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{m}$

The final diameter is $\mathrm{D}_{2}=6\mathrm{cm}\Rightarrow \mathrm{R}_{2}=3\mathrm{cm}=3\times 10^{-2}\mathrm{m}$

Substitute the values into the expression for work done :

$\mathrm{W}=8π(0.03)\left [\left (3\times 10^{-2}\right )^{2}-\left (1\times 10^{-2}\right )^{2}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{W}=0.24π\left [9\times 10^{-4}-1\times 10^{-4}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{W}=0.24π\left [8\times 10^{-4}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{W}=1.92π\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{J}=απ\times 10^{-4}\mathrm{J}$

$\Rightarrow α=1.92$

Therefore, the value of $α$ is 1.92 . 

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
A mixture of carbon dioxide and oxygen has volume $8310 cm^{3}$, temperature 300 K, pressure 100 kPa and mass 13.2 g. The number of moles of carbon dioxide and oxygen gases in the mixture respectively are $______$.
(Assume both carbon dioxide and oxygen gases behave like ideal gases) [R = 8.31 J/mol K]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Using the ideal gas equation $\mathrm{PV}=\mathrm{nRT}$

The pressure of gas is given as $\mathrm{P}=100\mathrm{kPa}=10^{5}\mathrm{Pa}$.

The volume of gas is $\mathrm{V}=8310\mathrm{cm}^{3}=8310\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{m}^{3}=8.31\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{m}^{3}$

The temperature of gas is $\mathrm{T}=300\mathrm{K}$

The universal gas constant is $\mathrm{R}=8.31\mathrm{J}/\mathrm{mol}.\mathrm{K}$

So, the number of moles of gas is,

$\mathrm{n}_{\text{total}}=\frac{\mathrm{PV}}{\mathrm{RT}}=\frac{10^{5}\times 8.31\times 10^{-3}}{8.31\times 300}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{n}_{\text{total}}=\frac{831}{2493}=\frac{1}{3}\approx 0.333\mathrm{moles}$

Let $\mathrm{n}_{1}$ be the moles of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{n}_{2}$ be the moles of $\mathrm{O}_{2},\mathrm{n}_{1}+\mathrm{n}_{2}=0.333$ .......(i) 

Molar mass of $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ is $\mathrm{M}_{1}=12+(2\times 16)=44\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{mol}$

Molar mass of $\mathrm{O}_{2}$ is $\mathrm{M}_{2}=2\times 16=32\mathrm{g}/\mathrm{mol}$

As the total mass of the mixture is 13.2 g :

$\mathrm{n}_{1}\mathrm{M}_{1}+\mathrm{n}_{2}\mathrm{M}_{2}=13.2$

$44n_{1}+32n_{2}=13.2\ldots ......(ii)$

From equation (i), $\mathrm{n}_{2}=0.333-\mathrm{n}_{1}$.

Substituting this into (ii) :

$44\mathrm{n}_{1}+32(0.333-\mathrm{n}_{1})=13.2$

$\Rightarrow$ $44n_{1}+10.66-32n_{1}=13.2$

$\Rightarrow$ $12n_{1}=2.54$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{n}_{1}\approx 0.21\text{moles}$

So, $\mathrm{n}_{2}=0.333-0.21=0.12$ moles

Therefore, the number of moles of carbon dioxide and oxygen gases in the mixture respectively are $0.21,0.12$. 

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift

text: If an air bubble of diameter 2 mm rises steadily through a liquid of density $2000 kg/m^{3}$ at a rate of 0.5 cm/s, then the coefficient of viscosity of liquid is $______$ Poise. (Take $g = 10 m/s^{2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
When the bubble rises steadily, the net force is zero. The forces involved are :


[IMG]


Buoyant force $(\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}})$ acting upwards: $\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}}=\mathrm{V}σ\mathrm{g}$, where $σ$ is liquid density and V is the volume of the bubble.

Weight ( $\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{g}}$ ) acting downwards: $\mathrm{W}=\mathrm{V}ρ\mathrm{g}$, where $ρ$ is air density.

Viscous drag $(\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{v}})$ acting downwards (opposing motion) : 

$\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{v}}=6πη\mathrm{rv}$, where $η$ is the viscosity of liquid, r is the radius of body and v is the speed.

As the bubble is rising steadily, so the net force acting on it should be zero.

Equating the forces :

$\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{B}}=\mathrm{W}+\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{v}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $Vσ\mathrm{g}=Vρ\mathrm{g}+6πη\mathrm{rv}$

Since the density of air ( $ρ$ ) is much smaller than the density of the liquid ( $σ=2000\mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}^{3}$ ), we can neglect W :

$\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}σg=6πηrv$

$\Rightarrow$ $η=\frac{2r^{2}σg}{9v}$

The radius of bubble is $\mathrm{r}=\frac{2\mathrm{mm}}{2}=1\mathrm{mm}=10^{-3}\mathrm{m}$

The density of liquid is $σ=2000\mathrm{kg}/\mathrm{m}^{3}$

The constant speed of rise of bubble is $\mathrm{v}=0.5\mathrm{cm}/\mathrm{s}=0.005\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}=5\times 10^{-3}\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$

And the acceleration due to gravity is $\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$

Putting the values,

$η=\frac{2\times \left (10^{-3}\right )^{2}\times 2000\times 10}{9\times 5\times 10^{-3}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $η=\frac{2\times 10^{-6}\times 2\times 10^{4}}{45\times 10^{-3}}=\frac{4\times 10^{-2}}{45\times 10^{-3}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $η=\frac{40}{45}\approx 0.888\mathrm{Pa}\cdot \mathrm{s}$

As Pa.s is the SI unit of viscosity and the required value is in CGS unit, Poise;

$1\mathrm{Pa}\cdot \mathrm{s}=10\text{Poise}\Rightarrow η=0.888\times 10=8.88\text{Poise}$

Therefore, the correct option is (B).

text:
A spherical ball of mass 2 kg falls from a height of 10 m and is brought to rest after penetrating 10 cm into sand.

 The average force exerted by sand on the ball is $_________ N$.

(Take $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Using the work-energy theorem, the work done by all forces acting on a body is equal to the change in its kinetic energy.

The ball falls from height $\mathrm{h}=10\mathrm{m}$ under gravity. And the ball enters the sand and travels a distance $\mathrm{d}=10\mathrm{cm}=0.1\mathrm{m}$ before coming to rest.

Let m be the mass of the ball, h be the initial height, d be the penetration depth, and $\mathrm{F}_{\text{avg}}$ be the average resistive force exerted by the sand.

The total work done on the ball from the moment it is dropped until it stops is:

$\mathrm{W}_{\text{total}}=\mathrm{W}_{\text{gravity}}+\mathrm{W}_{\text{sand}}$

Since the ball starts from rest at height $h$ and ends at rest after depth $d$, the total change in kinetic energy is zero $(\Delta \mathrm{K}=0)$.

$\mathrm{W}_{\text{gravity}}+\mathrm{W}_{\text{sand}}=0$

Gravity acts over the entire vertical displacement ( $\mathrm{h}+\mathrm{d}$ ).

So, the work done by gravitational force is $\mathrm{W}_{\text{gravity}}=\mathrm{mg}(\mathrm{h}+\mathrm{d})$

The resistive force $F_{\text{avg}}$ acts upwards, opposite to the displacement $d$.

So, the work done by the sand is $\mathrm{W}_{\text{sand}}=-\mathrm{F}_{\text{avg}}\cdot \mathrm{d}$

Substituting these into the energy equation :

$\mathrm{mg}(\mathrm{h}+\mathrm{d})-\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{avg}}\cdot \mathrm{d}=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{avg}}=\frac{\mathrm{mg}(\mathrm{h}+\mathrm{d})}{\mathrm{d}}$

The mass of ball is $\mathrm{m}=2\mathrm{kg}$, the height of fall is $\mathrm{h}=10\mathrm{m}$, the distance of penetration in sand is $\mathrm{d}=$ 0.1 m , and $\mathrm{g}=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

$\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{avg}}=\frac{2\times 10\times (10+0.1)}{0.1}$

$\Rightarrow$ $F_{avg}=\frac{20\times 10.1}{0.1}=20\times 101$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{avg}}=2020\mathrm{N}$

Therefore, the average force exerted by sand on the ball is 2020 N . 

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: An electromagnetic wave travels in free space along the x-direction. At a particular point in space and time, $⃗{B}=2\times 10^{-7}\hat{j}$ T is associated with this wave. The value of corresponding electric field $⃗{E}$ at this point is $_______ V/m$.

Wave travels along $+x$-direction

Magnetic field is  

$⃗{B}=2\times 10^{-7}\hat{j}\text{T}$

$⃗{E}\times ⃗{B}$

$E=cB$

where

$c=3\times 10^{8}\text{m/s}$

So,

$E=3\times 10^{8}\times 2\times 10^{-7}$

$E=6\times 10^{1}=60\text{V/m}$

Therefore,

$⃗{E}=-60\hat{k}\text{V/m}$

So, the correct answer is:

$-60\hat{k}\text{V/m}$

text: Two resistors of 200 $\Omega$ and 400 $\Omega$ are connected in series with a battery of 100 V. A bulb rated at 200 V, 100 W is connected across the 400 $\Omega$ resistance. The potential drop across the bulb is $________ V$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The bulb is rated at power $\mathrm{P}=100\mathrm{W}$ and the voltage rating is $\mathrm{V}_{\text{rated}}=200\mathrm{V}$.

Using the power formula $\mathrm{P}=\frac{\mathrm{V}^{2}}{\mathrm{R}}$, the resistance of the bulb is,

$\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{b}}=\frac{\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{rated}}^{2}}{\mathrm{P}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{b}}=\frac{(200)^{2}}{100}=\frac{40000}{100}=400\Omega$


[IMG]


The bulb $(400\Omega )$ is connected in parallel with the $400\Omega$ resistor. The equivalent resistance $(\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{p}})$ of two equal resistances in parallel is :

$\frac{1}{R_{p}}=\frac{1}{400}+\frac{1}{400}=\frac{2}{400}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{p}}=200\Omega$

This parallel combination is in series with the $200\Omega$ resistor.

$\mathrm{R}_{\text{total}}=200+\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{p}}=200+200=400\Omega$

So, the total current in the circuit is $\mathrm{i}=\frac{\mathrm{V}}{\mathrm{R}_{\text{total}}}=\frac{100}{400}=\frac{1}{4}\mathrm{A}$

As the bulb is in parallel with $400\Omega$ resistance, so the voltage drop across the bulb is same as across the parallel combination;

$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{bulb}}=\mathrm{iR}_{\mathrm{p}}=\frac{1}{4}\times 200\mathrm{V}=50\mathrm{V}$

Therefore, the potential drop across the bulb is 50 V. 

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
Two metal plates (A, B) are kept horizontally with separation of $\left (\frac{12}{π}\right )$ cm, with plate A on the top.

An atomizer jet sprays oil (density $1.5 g/cm^{3})$ droplets of radius 1 mm horizontally. All oil droplets carry a charge 5 nC. The potentials $V_{A}$ and $V_{B}$ are required on plates A and B respectively in order to ensure the droplets do not descend. The values of $V_{A}$ and $V_{B}$ are $______$.

(Neglect the air resistance to the droplets and take $g = 10 m/s^{2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a droplet of radius $r=10^{-3}\text{m}$ and density $ρ=1500\text{kg m}^{-3}$:

$m=\dfrac{4}{3}πr^{3}ρ=\dfrac{4}{3}π\left (10^{-9}\right )(1500)=2π\times 10^{-6}\text{kg}$

The droplet does not descend when the upward electric force balances its weight, $qE=mg$:

$E=\dfrac{mg}{q}=\dfrac{2π\times 10^{-6}\times 10}{5\times 10^{-9}}=4000π\text{V m}^{-1}$

With separation $d=\dfrac{12}{π}\text{cm}=\dfrac{0.12}{π}\text{m}$, the potential difference between the plates is

$\Delta V=Ed=4000π\times \dfrac{0.12}{π}=480\text{V}$

The charge is positive, so the force $q⃗{E}$ is upward only if $⃗{E}$ points upward, from the lower plate B to the upper plate A. The field points from higher to lower potential, so $V_{B}-V_{A}=480\text{V}$.

$V_{A}=100\text{V}$ and $V_{B}=580\text{V}$ satisfy this; the reverse pair (580 V and 100 V) has the same difference but a downward field.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: Two point charges $8μC$ and $-2μC$ are located at $x=2$ cm and $x=4$ cm, respectively on the $x$-axis. The ratio of electric flux due to these charges through two spheres of radii 3 cm and 5 cm with their centers at the origin is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Gauss's law states that the total electric flux $(𝜙)$ through any closed surface is given by :

$𝜙=\frac{\mathrm{q}_{\text{enclosed}}}{𝜖_{0}}$

Where $\mathrm{q}_{\text{enclosed}}$ is the net charge inside the surface and $𝜖_{0}$ is the permittivity of free space. Any charge located outside the closed surface does not contribute to the net flux through it.


[IMG]


The first sphere has a radius $\mathrm{R}_{1}=3\mathrm{cm}$ centreed at the origin.

Charge $\mathrm{q}_{1}=8μ\mathrm{C}$ is at $\mathrm{x}=2\mathrm{cm}$. So, charge $\mathrm{q}_{1}$ is inside $\mathrm{S}_{1}$.

Charge $\mathrm{q}_{2}=-2μ\mathrm{C}$ is at $\mathrm{x}=4\mathrm{cm}$. So, this charge is outside $\mathrm{S}_{1}$.

Thus, total charge enclosed by $\mathrm{S}_{1}$ is,

$\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{enc}1}=8μ\mathrm{C}$

Using Gauss law, the electric flux through sphere 1 is,

$𝜙_{1}=\frac{8μC}{𝜖_{0}}$

The second sphere has a radius $\mathrm{R}_{2}=5\mathrm{cm}$ centreed at the origin.

Charge $\mathrm{q}_{1}=8μ\mathrm{C}$ is at $\mathrm{x}=2\mathrm{cm}$. So, is inside $\mathrm{S}_{2}$.

Charge $\mathrm{q}_{2}=-2μ\mathrm{C}$ is at $\mathrm{x}=4\mathrm{cm}$. It is also inside $\mathrm{S}_{2}$.

Thus, total charge enclosed by $S_{2}$ is,

$q_{\text{enc}2}=8μC+(-2μC)=6μC$

Using Gauss law, the electric flux through sphere 2 is,

$𝜙_{2}=\frac{6μC}{𝜖_{0}}$

So, the ratio of electric flux through sphere 1 to sphere 2 is,

$\frac{𝜙_{1}}{𝜙_{2}}=\frac{8/𝜖_{0}}{6/𝜖_{0}}=\frac{8}{6}=\frac{4}{3}$

Therefore, the ratio of the electric flux is $4:3$. 

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
One side of an equilateral prism is painted by a transparent material of refractive index $n_{2}$. The refractive index of prism is $1.6$. The minimum value of $n_{2}$ required for total internal reflection from painted face is $________$.

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An equilateral prism has interior angles of $\mathrm{A}=60^{\circ }$.

The light ray enters the first face at a normal incidence (perpendicularly).

Angle of incidence at the first face $\mathrm{i}_{1}=0^{\circ }$.

By Snell's Law $\mathrm{n}_{1}\sin \mathrm{i}_{1}=\mathrm{n}_{2}\sin \mathrm{r}_{1}$, the angle of refraction $\mathrm{r}_{1}=0^{\circ }$.


[IMG]


In a prism, the relation between the apex angle $A$ and the internal angles is $A=r_{1}+r_{2}$.

$60^{\circ }=0^{\circ }+\mathrm{i}_{2}\Rightarrow \mathrm{i}_{2}=60^{\circ }$

The light ray strikes the painted face at an angle of $60^{\circ }$ relative to the normal.

For TIR to occur at the interface between the prism ( $\mathrm{n}_{\text{prism}}=1.6$ ) and the paint ( $\mathrm{n}_{2}$ ), the angle of incidence $\mathrm{i}_{2}$ must be greater than or equal to the critical angle $θ_{\mathrm{c}}$.

$\sin i_{2}\geq \sin θ_{c}$

The critical angle is defined by $\sin θ_{\mathrm{c}}=\frac{\mathrm{n}_{\text{rarer}}}{\mathrm{n}_{\text{denser}}}=\frac{\mathrm{n}_{2}}{\mathrm{n}_{\text{prism}}}$

$\sin 60^{\circ }\geq \frac{n_{2}}{1.6}$

Substituting the value of $\sin 60^{\circ }=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ :

$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\geq \frac{\mathrm{n}_{2}}{1.6}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{n}_{2}\leq \frac{1.6\times \sqrt{3}}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{n}_{2}\leq 0.8\sqrt{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{n}_{2}\leq \frac{4\sqrt{3}}{5}$

The maximum value $\mathrm{n}_{2}$ can take to ensure TIR is $\frac{4\sqrt{3}}{5}$. 

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text:
The figure given below shows an LCR series circuit with two switches $S_{1}$ and $S_{2}$. When switch $S_{1}$ is closed keeping $S_{2}$ open, the phase difference (φ) between the current and source voltage is 30° and phase difference is 60° when $S_{2}$ is closed keeping $S_{1}$ open. The value of $(3L_{1} − L_{2})$ is $______ H$.

[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In an LCR circuit the phase difference $𝜙$ is given by the formula :

$\tan 𝜙=\frac{|\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}}-\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}|}{\mathrm{R}}$

Case 1 : $\mathrm{S}_{1}$ closed, $\mathrm{S}_{2}$ open


[IMG]


In this case the inductor $\mathrm{L}_{2}$ is short-circuited. The active components are $\mathrm{R},\mathrm{C}$, and $\mathrm{L}_{1}$.

$\tan 30^{\circ }=\frac{\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{L}1}-\mathrm{X}_{\mathrm{C}}}{\mathrm{R}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{ω\mathrm{L}_{1}-\frac{1}{ω\mathrm{C}}}{\mathrm{R}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{R}=\sqrt{3}\left (ω\mathrm{L}_{1}-\frac{1}{ω\mathrm{C}}\right )......(ii)$

Case 2 : $S_{2}$ closed, $S_{1}$ open


[IMG]


Here, the inductor $L_{1}$ is short-circuited. The active components are $R,C$, and $L_{2}$.

$\tan 60^{\circ }=\frac{X_{L2}-X_{C}}{R}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\sqrt{3}=\frac{ω\mathrm{L}_{2}-\frac{1}{ω\mathrm{C}}}{\mathrm{R}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\mathrm{R}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\left (ω\mathrm{L}_{2}-\frac{1}{ω\mathrm{C}}\right ).......(ii)$

Equating both expressions for R :

$\sqrt{3}\left (ω\mathrm{L}_{1}-\frac{1}{ω\mathrm{C}}\right )=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\left (ω\mathrm{L}_{2}-\frac{1}{ω\mathrm{C}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $3ωL_{1}-\frac{3}{ωC}=ωL_{2}-\frac{1}{ωC}$

$\Rightarrow$ $3ωL_{1}-ωL_{2}=\frac{2}{ωC}$

$\Rightarrow$ $ω(3\mathrm{L}_{1}-\mathrm{L}_{2})=\frac{2}{ω\mathrm{C}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $3L_{1}-L_{2}=\frac{2}{ω^{2}C}$

Substituting $ω=300$ and $\mathrm{C}=100\times 10^{-6}\mathrm{F}$ :

$3\mathrm{L}_{1}-\mathrm{L}_{2}=\frac{2}{(300)^{2}\times 100\times 10^{-6}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $3\mathrm{L}_{1}-\mathrm{L}_{2}=\frac{2}{90000\times 10^{-4}}=\frac{2}{9}$

Therefore, the value of $3L_{1}-L_{2}$ is $\frac{2}{9}$. 

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: A circular current loop of radius $R$ is placed inside square loop of side length $L$ ($L\gg R$) such that they are co-planar and their centers coincide. The permeability of free space is $μ_{0}$. The mutual inductance between circular loop and square loop is $______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Mutual inductance M is defined by the flux $\Phi$ linked with one loop due to a current I in the other: $\Phi =\mathrm{MI}$.

It is easier to calculate the magnetic field produced by the larger square loop at the centre where the small circular loop is located.

A square loop consists of four wires of length $L$.

The distance from the centre to each wire is $r=\frac{L}{2}$.


[IMG]


The magnetic field at the centre due to one wire of length L is :

$\mathrm{B}_{\text{wire}}=\frac{μ_{0}\mathrm{I}}{4π\mathrm{r}}(\sin θ_{1}+\sin θ_{2})$

For a square centre, $θ_{1}=θ_{2}=45^{\circ }$ and $r=\frac{L}{2}$.

$B_{\text{wire}}=\frac{μ_{0}I}{4π(L/2)}\left (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right )=\frac{μ_{0}I}{2πL\left (\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right )}=\frac{μ_{0}I}{\sqrt{2}πL}$

Total field at the centre due to four such wires:

$B_{\text{total}}=4\times \frac{μ_{0}I}{\sqrt{2}πL}=\frac{2\sqrt{2}μ_{0}I}{πL}$

Since $L\gg R$, the magnetic field $B_{\text{total}}$ can be considered uniform over the area of the circular loop ($A=πR^{2}$).

$\Phi =B_{\text{total}}\times A$

$\Phi =\left (\frac{2\sqrt{2}μ_{0}I}{πL}\right )\times (πR^{2})=\frac{2\sqrt{2}μ_{0}R^{2}I}{L}$

Using $\Phi =\text{MI}$:

$\text{MI}=\frac{2\sqrt{2}μ_{0}R^{2}I}{L}$

$M=\frac{2\sqrt{2}μ_{0}R^{2}}{L}$

Therefore, the mutual inductance between circular loop and square loop is $\frac{2\sqrt{2}μ_{0}R^{2}}{L}$. Thus, the correct option is (D)

text:
The binding energy per nucleon of ${}_{83}^{209}Bi$ is $_______$ MeV.
[Take $m(_{83}^{209}Bi)=208.980388\text{u}$, $m_{p}=1.007825\text{u}$, $m_{n}=1.008665\text{u}$, $1\text{u}=931\text{MeV}/c^{2}$]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The mass defect is the difference between the sum of the masses of the individual nucleons (protons and neutrons) and the actual mass of the nucleus.

For $\text{Bi}_{83}^{209}$:

Number of protons (Z) $=83$

Number of neutrons (N) $=A-Z=209-83=126$

$\Delta m=[Zm_{p}+Nm_{n}]-M_{\text{nucleus}}$

$\Delta m=[83\times 1.007825+126\times 1.008665]-208.980388$

$\Delta m=[83.649475+127.09179]-208.980388$

$\Delta m=210.741265-208.980388=1.760877\text{u}$

Using Einstein's mass-energy equivalence, the binding energy is:

$\text{B.E.}=\Delta m\times 931\text{MeV/u}$

$\text{B.E.}=1.760877\times 931\approx 1639.376\text{MeV}$

The binding energy per nucleon is the total binding energy divided by the mass number (A $=209$).

$\frac{\text{B.E.}}{A}=\frac{1639.376}{209}\approx 7.8439\text{MeV}$

Therefore, the binding energy per nucleon of $\text{Bi}_{83}^{209}$ is $7.8439\text{MeV}$. Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: The equation of motion of a particle is given by $x=a\sin (50t+π/3)$ cm. The particle will come to rest at time $t_{1}$ and it will have zero acceleration at time $t_{2}$. The $t_{1}$ and $t_{2}$ respectively are $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The velocity $v$ is the first derivative of displacement $x$ with respect to time $t$.

$v=\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}\left [a\sin \left (50t+\frac{π}{3}\right )\right ]$

$v=50a\cos \left (50t+\frac{π}{3}\right )$

The particle comes to rest when $v=0$.

$50a\cos \left (50t_{1}+\frac{π}{3}\right )=0\Rightarrow \cos \left (50t_{1}+\frac{π}{3}\right )=0$

The first positive time occurs when the phase is $\frac{π}{2}$:

$50t_{1}+\frac{π}{3}=\frac{π}{2}$

$50t_{1}=\frac{π}{2}-\frac{π}{3}=\frac{π}{6}$

$t_{1}=\frac{π}{300}s$

The acceleration $a$ is the derivative of velocity $v$.

$a=\frac{dv}{dt}=\frac{d}{dt}\left [50a\cos \left (50t+\frac{π}{3}\right )\right ]$

$a=-2500a\sin \left (50t+\frac{π}{3}\right )$

Acceleration is zero when $\sin \left (50t_{2}+\frac{π}{3}\right )=0$.

The first positive time (other than the initial state if it is zero) occurs when the phase is $π$:

$50t_{2}+\frac{π}{3}=π$

$50t_{2}=π-\frac{π}{3}=\frac{2π}{3}$

$t_{2}=\frac{2π}{150}=\frac{π}{75}s$

Therefore, the particle will come to rest time $\frac{π}{300}\mathrm{s}$ and it will have zero acceleration at time $\mathrm{t}_{2}\frac{π}{75}\mathrm{s}$. Thus, the correct option is (A).

text: In a Young's double slit experiment, the intensity at some point on the screen is found to be $\frac{3}{4}$ times of the maximum of the interference pattern. The path difference between the interfering waves at this point is $\frac{λ}{x}$ where $λ$ is wavelength of the incident light. The value of $x$ is $_______$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The resultant intensity $I$ at a point where two waves of equal intensity $I_{0}$ interfere is given by:

$I=I_{\text{\max }}\cos ^{2}\left (\frac{𝜙}{2}\right )$

Where $I_{\text{\max }}$ is the maximum intensity $(4I_{0})$ and $𝜙$ is the phase difference between the waves.

The intensity at some point on screen is given as $I=\frac{3}{4}I_{\text{\max }}$:

$\frac{3}{4}I_{\text{\max }}=I_{\text{\max }}\cos ^{2}\left (\frac{𝜙}{2}\right )$

$\cos ^{2}\left (\frac{𝜙}{2}\right )=\frac{3}{4}$

$\cos \left (\frac{𝜙}{2}\right )=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$\frac{𝜙}{2}=\frac{π}{6}$

$𝜙=\frac{π}{3}$

The phase difference $𝜙$ is related to the path difference $\Delta p$ by the formula:

$𝜙=\frac{2π}{λ}\Delta p$

Substituting the value of $𝜙$:

$\frac{π}{3}=\frac{2π}{λ}\Delta p$

$\Delta p=\frac{π}{3}\times \frac{λ}{2π}$

$\Delta p=\frac{λ}{6}=\frac{λ}{x}⟹x=6$

Therefore, the value of $x$ is 6. So, the correct answer is 6.

text: Using Bohr’s model, calculate the ratio of the magnetic fields generated due to the motion of the electrons in the $2^{nd}$ and $4^{th}$ orbits of hydrogen atom $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An electron of charge $e$ moving with speed $v$ in an orbit of radius $r$ is a current loop carrying

$i=\dfrac{e}{T}=\dfrac{ev}{2πr}$

The magnetic field at the centre of the orbit is

$B=\dfrac{μ_{0}i}{2r}=\dfrac{μ_{0}ev}{4πr^{2}}$

In Bohr's model of hydrogen, $v\propto \dfrac{1}{n}$ and $r\propto n^{2}$, so

$B\propto \dfrac{1/n}{n^{4}}=\dfrac{1}{n^{5}}$

For the 2nd and 4th orbits,

$\dfrac{B_{2}}{B_{4}}=\left (\dfrac{4}{2}\right )^{5}=32$

Hence, the answer is 32.

text: 5 moles of unknown gas is heated at constant volume from 10°C to 20°C. The molar specific heat of this gas at constant pressure $c_{p}=8$ cal/mol.°C and $R=8.36$ J/mol.°C. The change in the internal energy of the gas is $__________$ calorie.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Using Mayer’s relation for an ideal gas, the relationship between molar specific heat at constant pressure $(C_{p})$ and constant volume $(C_{v})$ is given by:

$C_{p}-C_{v}=R$

The gas constant $R$ is in terms of joules, we need to convert it to $\frac{\text{cal}}{\text{mol}\cdot ^{\circ }C}$.

We know that $1\text{cal}\approx 4.18\text{J}$.

$R=\frac{8.36\text{J/mol}\cdot ^{\circ }C}{4.18\text{J/cal}}=\frac{2\text{cal}}{\text{mol}\cdot ^{\circ }C}$

Now, substituting the values into Mayer's relation:

$8-C_{v}=2$

$C_{v}=\frac{6\text{cal}}{\text{mol}\cdot ^{\circ }C}$

The change in internal energy for $n$ moles of gas when its temperature changes by $\Delta T$ is:

$\Delta U=nC_{v}\Delta T$

The amount of gas is $n=5$ moles

The change in temperature is

$\Delta T=T_{\text{final}}-T_{\text{initial}}=20^{\circ }C-10^{\circ }C=10^{\circ }C$

Putting the values,

$\Delta U=5\times 6\times 10$

$\Delta U=300\text{calories}$

Therefore, the change in internal energy of the gas is 300 Calories. Thus, the correct answer is 300.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift

text: If sunlight is focused on a paper using convex lens, it starts burning the paper in shortest time when the lens is kept at 30 cm above the paper. If the radius of curvature of the lens is 60 cm then the refractive index of the lens material is $\frac{α}{10}$. The value of $α$ is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 2nd April Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Since the source (sun) is at infinity, sunlight consists of parallel rays. A convex lens converges parallel rays at its principal focus. Therefore, if the paper burns at a distance of 30 cm, this distance represents the focal length of the lens.

$f=30\text{cm}$

For a thin lens with radii of curvature $R_{1}$ and $R_{2}$, the focal length and refractive index $μ$ are related by Lens makers formula:

$\frac{1}{f}=(μ-1)\left (\frac{1}{R_{1}}-\frac{1}{R_{2}}\right )$

Assuming the lens is a equi-convex, then $R_{1}=+R$ and $R_{2}=-R$.

$\frac{1}{f}=(μ-1)\left (\frac{1}{R}-\frac{1}{-R}\right )=(μ-1)\left (\frac{2}{R}\right )$

$μ-1=\frac{R}{2f}$

The radius of curvature is given as $R=60\text{cm}$ and $f=30\text{cm}$:

$μ-1=\frac{60}{2\times 30}=\frac{60}{60}=1$

$μ=1+1=2$

$\Rightarrow 2=\frac{α}{10}$

$\Rightarrow α=20$

Therefore, the value of $α$ is 20. Thus, the final answer is 20.

Moment of inertia about an axis AB for a rod of mass 40 kg and length 3 m is same as that of a solid sphere of mass of 10 kg and radius $R$ about an axis parallel to AB axis with separation of 3 m as shown in figure below. The value of $R$ is given as $\sqrt{\frac{α}{2}}$. The value of $α$ is $________$.


[IMG]

solution.body:
For the rod:

The axis $AB$ passes through the end of the rod. The moment of inertia of a uniform rod of mass $M$ and length $L$ about an axis passing through one of its ends is given by:

$I_{\text{rod}}=\frac{1}{3}ML^{2}$

The mass of rod is $M=40\text{kg}$ and $L=3\text{m}$:

$I_{\text{rod}}=\frac{1}{3}\times 40\times (3)^{2}=\frac{1}{3}\times 40\times 9=120\text{kg}\cdot \text{m}^{2}$

For the sphere:

The axis for the sphere is parallel to $AB$ at a distance $d=3\text{m}$ from its centre.

According to the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia $I$ about any axis is:

$I=I_{\text{cm}}+Md^{2}$

For a solid sphere, the moment of inertia about its centre of mass is $I_{\text{cm}}=\frac{2}{5}mR^{2}$.

The mass of sphere is $m=10\text{kg}$ and $d=3\text{m}$:

Putting the values,

$I_{\text{sphere}}=\left (\frac{2}{5}\times 10\times R^{2}\right )+(10\times 3^{2})$

$I_{\text{sphere}}=4R^{2}+90$

It is given that, $I_{\text{rod}}=I_{\text{sphere}}$.

$120=4R^{2}+90$

$4R^{2}=120-90$

$4R^{2}=30$

$R^{2}=\frac{30}{4}=\frac{15}{2}$

$R=\sqrt{\frac{15}{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{α}{2}}\Rightarrow α=15$

Therefore, the value of $α$ is 15. Thus, the correct answer is $\text{15}.$
